newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish govt to buy some surplus sugar for reserves.
newsitem.headline: Polish govt to buy some surplus sugar for reserves.

text.p: The Polish government is planning to buy an undisclosed amount of sugar from the country's expected 400,000-tonne production surplus this year for state reserves, a deputy agriculture minister said on Tuesday.

Jerzy Pilarczyk told a news briefing after a cabinet meeting that some of the surplus sugar, otherwise destined for unsubsidised export -- called the C quota -- could be bought by the country's food market regulator, the state-run Agriculture Market Agency (ARR).
"The government plans to purchase some sugar from the C quota for state and ARR reserves...it will be one of the ways to solve the problem of sugar overproduction," Pilarczyk said.
Poland's white sugar output is expected to rise to between two and 2.1 million tonnes in 1996, from 1.58 million in 1995.
Poland will subsidise exports of 118,300 tonnes of sugar in 1997 and its domestic use is estimated at 1.5 million tonnes.
